audits.jarvis_gap: The run-06 program genuinely closed the audit-attribution, migration-chain-CI, verdict-source, and permission-seed gaps, and it genuinely activated two brand-new durable ledgers (public.infra_conditions for the reliability lifecycle, and the wake-capable public.delegation_ledger for cross-butler delegation) with real producers, race-safe reconciliation, and CI-enforced regression guards -- this is not skin-deep. The gap is the next hop of the trace spine: both ledgers write real evidence-backed rows now, but neither has a dashboard door. infra_conditions has zero API router and zero frontend surface, so an L0->L3 escalating outage is durable in Postgres but invisible to the owner except via psql. delegation_ledger has an existing read-only API and it is wired to nothing in the frontend (dead door, unused since bu-gxmfx), and even if it were rendered, the API model was never extended to expose the new wake_state/wake_key/wake_task_id columns #3535 added -- so a delegated ask that silently lands in wake_state=callback_failed or task_conflict (the two failure states #3535 introduces) would show as an ordinary 'answered' row with no sign the asker never actually got woken. The ideal is that every new durable ledger this program creates ships together with (a) a dashboard panel or drill-down and (b) full column parity in whatever read API backs it, so the trace spine's 'evidence' link is never a table only a shell command can reach.

findings.detail: Issues (the signal) is bus-primary with a fast-fallback reconciliation poll when the socket drops. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the Attention & Action trio (Notifications/Approvals/Decisions) is unusually mature for a JARVIS pursuit surface: Approvals is a genuine One Trust Console with expiry/blast-radius ranking, session-trace links on every dossier, an undo-windowed keyboard triage loop, and a full standing-autonomy ledger; Notifications carries proper source_available em-dashing and a URL-backed filter/verdict-opener pair; Decisions just landed (bu-27dxl.8.5) a read-only structured projection with honest degraded-envelope handling. The ideal is not "build this from scratch" but "finish flattening it into one dialect and one recovery contract": every row across all three surfaces should share the identical header chrome and Title primitive, every irreversible bulk action should carry the same confirm/undo contract the single-item actions already have, and every signal -- including a Decisions row's own id and the bead it is escalation-blocking -- should be a door onto the same evidence spine (session, trace, or source bead) that Notifications and Approvals already wired for their own rows. Closing those three residual gaps is what turns \"three well-built pages\" into \"one Trust Console family.\"

findings.title: Bulk 'Acknowledge all failed' has no confirm and no undo, unlike every other risky control on this surface
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/NotificationsPage.tsx:279-281,350-361; frontend/src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:99-111
findings.detail: handleAcknowledgeAll fires useAcknowledgeAllFailed() straight from the click handler with no confirmation. useAcknowledgeAllFailed is a plain useOptimisticListMutation: it optimistically flips every cached 'failed' notification to 'read' and only rolls back on a network error -- never on user regret; there is no undo toast/window. This is the one unbounded-blast-radius bulk action on the whole surface (it can silently clear an arbitrary number of failure signals) yet it is the only control with neither confirm nor undo: ApprovalsPage's keyboard approve/deny/defer verbs route through an explicit UNDO_WINDOW_MS scheduled-decision + toast (ApprovalsPage.tsx:84-100), and Notifications' own single mark-read is low-blast-radius (one row, easily re-flagged). Design-bar Recovery bias: 'require explicit confirmation where [an action] is not [reversible] -- never replace a confirm with an undo that can't undo.' This control has neither.

findings.title: Decisions rows are fully unlinked: no door from a decision to its source bead, evidence, or the item it is blocking
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DecisionsPage.tsx:99-219 (decision.id, escalated_blocked_id, escalated_blocked_title all render as plain text/spans, zero <a>/<Link> in the file); frontend/src/api/types.ts:8845-8870 (DecisionBeadSummary has no session_id/trace_id/external-URL field)

audits.jarvis_gap: The memory surface (bu-2ix8d house-ledger redesign) is one of the most disciplined pages in the app: every list/stat query distinguishes a genuine empty state from a fetch error via explicit isError checks and MemoryLoadError, degraded-fan-out sources are named inline rather than silently undercounted, and color is confined to a single rail. The remaining gap is not truthfulness of data but continuity of the trace spine once the owner leaves the register: the three detail pages' breadcrumbs hardcode a bare `/memory` (or `/memory?register=X`) href that discards whatever validity/maturity/status filter got the owner there, so a drill-down from an attention-rail action (e.g. "review" -> fading facts, anti-pattern rules, dead-letter episodes) does not round-trip back to that filtered view via the page's own back door — only the browser back button does. Separately, two of the rail's five attention conditions (important-fading facts, stale embeddings) quietly fall back to 0 on a fetch error instead of the isError-aware treatment used one function up for stats/activity, and the page's one mutating hot loop (Confirm/Retract on the fact detail commit footer) has no command-palette or keyboard entry even though HousekeepingBand's mutations on the same page do.

findings.title: Health hub sub-pages split into two incompatible header dialects
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/MeasurementsPage.tsx:9-17, MedicationsPage.tsx:18-25, MealsPage.tsx:158-165 build a bespoke `Eyebrow` (mono) + `Display` (large headline component) + `Voice` (serif lead) header; frontend/src/pages/ConditionsPage.tsx, SymptomsPage.tsx, ResearchPage.tsx instead wrap in `<Page archetype="list" title=... description=...>` (frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx) which renders via `Title as="h1"` (frontend/src/components/ui/Title.tsx:1-8, documented "Inter Tight, 24px, weight 500") plus a plain description paragraph — no mono Eyebrow, no serif Voice lead, no Display-scale headline.
findings.detail: Three of the six sibling record surfaces under one hub (Measurements, Medications, Meals) render the editorial Dispatch header (large Display headline + serif Voice paragraph), while the other three (Conditions, Symptoms, Research) render the generic dashboard Page shell's smaller Title h1 + plain description — a visible size/typeface/voice mismatch between pages one hop apart in the same ledger index (HealthLedgerIndex.tsx). This is drift beyond the already-tracked Card→Tile consolidation (bu-27dxl.12); it's inconsistent header composition within a single domain hub, violating "one visual language built by one hand."

audits.ideal: A world-class Health hub treats every signal as a door with a key: an attention-list item for "missed 2 doses of Metformin" lands directly on that medication's row, pre-scrolled and briefly highlighted, in the same way the measurement domain's typed door already threads type/since/until into the Measurements URL — every one of the six record categories gets the same typed-door contract, not just measurements. The domain's actual hot loop — log a dose, log a meal, add a reading, note a symptom — is reachable in two keystrokes from anywhere in the hub via the command palette (mirroring the read-only refresh commands already registered on the overview page), so the owner never has to reach for a mouse to record data mid-conversation with their butler. And all six sibling record pages, one hop from the same ledger index, share one literal header component instantiation (Eyebrow + Display + Voice) rather than splitting three-and-three across two different page shells with different type scales — so navigating the ledger never produces a jarring typographic gear-shift.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the Health overview is genuinely strong — no fabricated numbers, every source-error state is named and retryable, KPI staleness is SLA-tinted rather than presented as calm, and the measurement domain has a real typed deep-link door from insight to filtered chart. But that rigor stops at the measurement boundary: the other five record domains (medications, conditions, symptoms, meals, research) receive insight links that dead-end on an unfiltered list, and none of the six record surfaces expose their primary write action (log/add) to the keyboard or palette, forcing the domain's actual daily hot loop through the mouse only. A visible seam also splits the hub's own six pages into two unrelated header dialects. None of these are covered by the in-flight bu-27dxl program, which is focused on chronicles, provenance, delegation, and reliability rather than this specific domain's completion.

findings.title: TopSessionsSection and ByScheduleSection replace good cached data with an error message on a transient background-poll failure
findings.evidence:
frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:883-884 (`isError ?

Failed to load top sessions.

`) and :989-990 (`isError ?

Failed to load schedule costs.

`), both checked before the `sessions.length`/`schedules.length` branches. Contrast with BreakdownSection (SpendPage.tsx:759, `isError && entries.length === 0`) and SpendRulesSection (:1526, `isError && rules.length === 0`), which explicitly gate the degraded-source render on 'nothing cached' per the bu-mkd5r three-way state contract cited in their own comments (:760-763, :1527-1531). useTopSessions/useCostsBySchedule (hooks/use-spend.ts:122-155) are plain useQuery calls, so React Query keeps the last-good `data` across a failed background refetch (poll interval from useBusAwarePollInterval) while flipping `isError` true — meaning a single transient poll failure blanks a populated, correct evidence table with plain unstyled text (no SourceDegradedNote, no retry action), even though the real rows are still sitting in cache.

findings.title: Routing-rule reordering is drag-only with no keyboard equivalent
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1153-1200 (RulesTable): each TableRow has `draggable`, `onDragStart`, `onDrop`, `onDragOver` (:1169-1173) and no `tabIndex`, `onKeyDown`, `role="button"`, or `aria-grabbed`/`aria-roledescription` anywhere in the file (confirmed via grep — zero matches for these attributes in SpendPage.tsx). Reordering routing rules is not decorative: rules evaluate top-to-bottom with 'first match wins' (:1148, :1496) and directly change which model/cap a dispatch is routed to — a real hot loop with live spend consequences that a keyboard-only or switch-access operator cannot perform at all.

findings.title: Token-divergence evidence is aggregated into an opaque count with no drill-down, even though the API already carries the exact coordinates
findings.evidence: SpendDivergence (frontend/src/api/types.ts:627-633) carries `date`, `butler`, `ledger_tokens`, `session_tokens`, `difference_ratio` — enough to point at exactly which day-butler bucket disagrees. Every render site collapses this to a bare count string with no link and no per-bucket listing: SpendPage.tsx:807-813 (`ledger/session token drift in ${divergenceCount} day-butler bucket(s)`), :2047-2054 (forecast chart footnote, same phrasing), :2116-2123 (daily chart footnote, same phrasing). None of the three SourceDegradedNote calls pass a link, an expandable detail, or route to a filtered Top-Sessions/By-Schedule view for the offending butler+date — the owner is told a real discrepancy exists and then has no door to the sessions that caused it, breaking the signal->session->evidence trace spine for the one condition that is explicitly about ledger truthfulness.

findings.title: Routing rule 'Saved 7d' figure has no evidence trail
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1182-1184 renders `rule.saved_7d` as plain tabular text (`fmtUsdPrecise(rule.saved_7d)`) with no Link — unlike every other dollar figure that touches a butler on this page (MoverChip :565-566, BreakdownBar :672-675, TopSessionsSection butler cell :914-916, ByScheduleSection butler cell :1025-1027 all link through to `/butlers/:name?tab=spend`). A rule's headline savings claim is asserted with no path to the dispatches/sessions it was computed from, so the owner cannot verify why a given rule is credited with saving a specific dollar amount.

audits.ideal: A world-class Spend console tells the owner, within one glance, whether they are on budget, what changed, and why — and every one of those three answers is a door, never a dead end: the movers strip, the honest per-butler-per-day chart, top sessions, by-schedule projections, and routing rules all already do this well by linking straight to `/butlers/:name?tab=spend` or `/sessions/:id`. The remaining gap is trust under stress: a transient poll hiccup must never replace a populated, correct table with a bare error line (it should keep showing the last-good evidence with a small degraded footnote and a retry action, exactly as BreakdownSection and SpendRulesSection already do); a flagged ledger/session divergence must resolve to the exact day-butler buckets and the sessions inside them, not just a count; a routing rule's claimed savings must be traceable to the sessions it altered; and every action that changes live routing — reordering, deleting, editing a rule — must be fully keyboard-operable, with the drag affordance as a bonus not a requirement. Get those four things right and this page becomes what it already almost is: a single honest surface where 'am I on budget, what changed, why, and can I act on it' all resolve in the same continuous motion, with no rendered number the owner cannot chase back to its session.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today's Spend page is unusually mature relative to most surfaces audited in this pursuit — it already implements the three-way degraded-source state contract (loading / real-empty / source-error, never conflating a failure with a genuine $0), fabricated-calm guards on ceiling_source_error, unavailable-butler footnoting across every fan-out, and a fleet-halt banner for the single most consequential spend signal. The gap that remains is narrower but real: two of the evidence-layer sections (Top Sessions, By Schedule) didn't inherit the same 'keep cached data visible through a transient error' discipline the rest of the page enforces, so a routine poll blip can hide correct evidence behind a plain error string; the drift/divergence signal that exists specifically to catch ledger dishonesty is itself reported as an unclickable count even though the API already carries per-bucket date+butler coordinates; keyboard operability was never extended to the one control on this page that changes live dispatch routing (rule reordering); and a routing rule's advertised savings has no evidence door. None of these are fabrication — they are trace-spine and resilience gaps on an otherwise honest surface.

audits.ideal: The ideal settings/secrets surface is a single trust ledger: every tile on /settings, every row in /settings/permissions, /settings/models, and /secrets carries a provable state — ok, degraded-with-last-known, or hard-failed — and never silently downgrades "I could not check" into "there is nothing to see." Every fetch failure (audit reel, webhook list, permission matrix, credential inventory) surfaces the same SourceDegradedNote/Retry vocabulary already used for spend and approvals, so the owner never mistakes network flakiness for an actually-empty audit trail or an actually-disabled webhook. Every list item — a webhook, a permission cell, a model, a credential — is one hop (click or palette command) from its underlying evidence: the audit-log entry that explains a permission flip, the last probe result behind a model's verified badge, the last delivery attempt behind a webhook's status dot. The whole surface is keyboard-navigable and palette-addressable end to end (reload, retry, export, add-webhook are already there; the gaps are just the couple of panels that quietly forgot the isError branch), so a five-second glance at /settings plus one keypress is enough to know whether access control, spend, models, and credentials are all in the state the owner believes they are in.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today, three of four fetches on the Permissions page (audit reel, webhook list, and — to a lesser extent, since it does show a failure message but with no recovery path — the permission matrix) do not treat a query failure as a distinct render state from "empty." Two of them (audit reel, webhooks) fully collapse failure into the calm "nothing here" empty copy, meaning a Switchboard/DB outage on this specific page reads as "no privileged actions have happened" and "no webhooks are configured" — exactly the fabricated-calm failure mode the fleet has already been eliminating everywhere else on the dashboard (spend, approvals, decisions, notifications, secrets inventory all already got this treatment). The rest of the surface (SettingsConsolePage panels, SettingsModelsPage, SecretsPage/DirectionPassport) is in solid, disciplined shape — proper isError branches, SourceDegradedNote usage, and palette command registration are the norm, which is exactly why these two leftover instances stand out as the gap rather than a systemic failure.

audits.jarvis_gap: The Education page already carries a well-built page-level error/empty/loading three-way contract (EducationPage.tsx:88-127) and a prior honesty pass (bu-occhw) fixed QuizHistoryList and MasterySummaryCards specifically — but that fix was never generalized to the rest of the surface. Four of the page's core widgets (concept graph, mastery trend chart, cross-topic chart, struggling-concepts card) still drop `isError` and fall through to a calm empty/no-data render, so a genuine backend outage on the selected curriculum's data reads as 'nothing wrong here' instead of 'we don't know.' Layered on top, the surface's color system is fractured: half the mastery/status badges use the Dispatch `var(--green)/var(--amber)/var(--red)` tokens (matching the spec) and the other half use raw Tailwind literals (`bg-blue-100`, `bg-slate-100`, `bg-purple-100`, `border-l-red-500`) the design-language spec explicitly forbids outside the token file. The ideal version would treat every query on this page as one honest three-state contract (loading/error/empty, never conflated), render every mastery/quality/status badge from one shared token-driven component so 'mastered' and 'blackout' mean the same color everywhere in the app, and give the Reviews queue (a genuine daily hot loop) a keyboard path to move through pending items without a mouse.

findings.evidence: Token-correct: MindMapGraph.tsx:22-28 (`STATUS_COLORS` using `var(--green)`, `var(--mfg)`, `var(--amber)`, `var(--dim)`, `var(--border-strong)`); QuizHistoryList.tsx:9-15 (partial — quality 0/1/2/3/5 use `var(--red)`/`var(--amber)`/`var(--green)` tokens). audits.jarvis_gap: The QA surface has already absorbed multiple prior JARVIS rounds (bu-533qx, bu-86c4c.19, bu-hmdqz.9, bu-qvnce.11): it has honest tri-state breaker rendering, evidence-bearing confirms, real trace-spine doors to /sessions/:id, degraded-source notes for the patrol strip, and stage-aware PR/diagnosis empty states that refuse to fabricate progress. What remains is not structural but four concrete cracks: an investigation-detail route that collapses 'case genuinely absent' and 'source unreachable' into the same 'not found' sentence (breaking the earned-calm distinction the rest of the page enforces), a live-in-progress patrol detail view that never repolls so a running patrol looks permanently frozen, a stray window.confirm on Force Patrol sitting right next to the AlertDialog the fleet already built to replace that exact pattern for the breaker, and a case rail with no keyboard roving-index despite every sibling list surface (Sessions, Issues, Approvals, Notifications, Decisions, AuditLog, Dashboard) having adopted the shared use-list-triage hook for exactly this hot loop.

findings.title: Investigation-detail route renders 'not found' for both absent case and unreachable source
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/QaInvestigationDetailPage.tsx:28-48
findings.detail: Two separate branches -- one for 'no data, no error' (legitimately absent case) and one for 'isError' (source genuinely unreachable) -- render the identical string 'Investigation not found.' This conflates a proven-absent case with a proven-unreachable staffer. Every other surface on this page distinguishes the two deliberately (QaOverviewPage.tsx:768-771 'Couldn't reach the staffer.' vs 772-775 'Nothing in the dossier.'; CaseDossier.tsx:74-79 'QA dossier unavailable.' for isError vs the loading/select branches). An operator who lands on /qa/investigations/:id via a stale link or bookmark during a staffer outage is told the case doesn't exist, when in fact the evidence for it is simply unreachable -- the exact fabricated-absence failure mode the rest of this page was built to avoid.
findings.failure_scenario: Staffer backend goes unreachable for a minute; operator opens a bookmarked /qa/investigations/:id link and is told 'Investigation not found', concluding the case was deleted/never existed, when it in fact still exists and the source is merely down.

findings.title: "Stop generation" does not stop generation — it only stops the client from watching
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:343-345 (handleStop calls abortRef.current?.abort() only); frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:356-358 (identical); backend src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:288 (_submit_to_switchboard dispatches the envelope to the routed butler's own independently-scheduled ephemeral session) and :361 (the SSE generator's only reaction to client disconnect is `if await request.is_disconnected(): ... return` — it stops the poll loop, never the routed butler's session)
findings.detail: The SSE endpoint this request talks to is a pure poller: it submits the envelope once, then loops calling message_find_reply_since() against a reply the ROUTED BUTLER's own session writes independently and asynchronously. Aborting the fetch on the client, or the server detecting request.is_disconnected(), only ends this HTTP connection's poll loop — nothing signals the underlying butler session to stop. The owner presses a button labeled "Stop generation" with a square icon, sees the bubble mark "Interrupted" and vanish 1.5s later (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:317-321), and reasonably concludes the system stopped working. In reality the routed butler keeps running to completion, keeps spending tokens/cost, and will still persist a reply — the UI just stops listening for it. This is a control fabrication: the interface promises an ability (interrupt) the system does not have, the mirror image of the fabricated-calm sins already fixed elsewhere (bu-27dxl.7) but on the send/stop path rather than the read path. A returning owner who reopens the conversation later will find a reply they believed they cancelled.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner sends a message that triggers a slow/expensive multi-tool butler session, clicks Stop after 2s believing it halted, closes the tab — the session keeps running for minutes, consumes real LLM spend, and silently writes a reply the owner never sees or wanted, with zero UI trace that it happened.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/StateDot.tsx:56 (canonical STATE_COLORS is a private const, not exported); frontend/src/components/topology/TopologyGraph.tsx:56,68,81,88 (four parallel maps STATUS_COLORS/STAFFER_STATUS_COLORS/TONE_COLORS/STAFFER_TONE_COLORS in one file); frontend/src/components/overview/BriefingStatus.tsx:65 (DOT_COLORS Record); frontend/src/components/sessions/ToolCallTimeline.tsx:125-129 (TOOL_CALL_OUTCOME_STYLES); frontend/src/components/system/ButlerHeartbeatTile.tsx:44 (dotClassFor); frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/atoms.tsx:20 (toneColor); frontend/src/lib/qa-patrol-status.ts:12 (dotClassName); frontend/src/components/layout/LiveIndicator.tsx:36-46; frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardFooter.tsx:116,123; frontend/src/components/sessions/StatusBadge.tsx:40
findings.detail: The dataviz layer has an exemplary single-source color registry (lib/chart-colors.ts, four documented channels), but the semantic status→token mapping (healthy/degraded/error/success/pending → green/amber/red/muted) has no equivalent. StateDot already encodes the canonical map but keeps it private (const, not export). Every consuming surface therefore re-derives the same mapping independently, in divergent expression forms (Tailwind class `bg-[var(--green)]`, CSS var string `var(--green)`, `bg-destructive`, `bg-muted-foreground/40`). This is a pattern built once (StateDot's STATE_COLORS) but never generalized — the classic drift vector. Distinct from bu-27dxl.12 'one StateDot', which unifies the dot RENDER primitive; these maps also feed badge borders, text, timeline nodes and rails that a dot component does not cover.

findings.title: Status-dot diameter has no size token; ad-hoc dots span 6/8/10px
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/StateDot.tsx:52 (default size 6); ad-hoc dots at h-1.5 w-1.5 (6px) frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:112; h-2 w-2 (8px) frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerApprovalsTab.tsx:89 and pages/SpendPage.tsx:572; size-2 (8px) frontend/src/components/topology/TopologyGraph.tsx:368; h-2.5 w-2.5 (10px) frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerChroniclerTimelinesTab.tsx:287
findings.detail: The Dispatch spec fixes the status dot at 6px (StateDot brief §2), but ~54 ad-hoc dots across ~25 files use three different diameters with no shared token. Even once bu-27dxl.12 migrates callers onto StateDot, StateDot's own `size` prop is a free number with no scale — nothing prevents the next divergence. A named dot-size token (or removing the size prop for a fixed 6px + one explicit 'lg' variant) closes it.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the Butlers frontend has a genuinely mature visual language at the token and dataviz layers: index.css is a comprehensive, well-annotated token file with semantic surface/state/severity/category/tier ramps; raw hex leaks are effectively eliminated (every apparent hit is a bead-ID comment or a color-input placeholder); and lib/chart-colors.ts is an exemplary single-source registry with four documented, non-cross-wired channels that every chart actually routes through (no chart bypasses it with a raw --chart-N or hardcoded stroke). The gap to world-class is the missing middle layer: the semantic status→token mapping. There is a canonical map — but it lives privately inside StateDot (STATE_COLORS, not exported), so ~15 surfaces each hand-roll their own status/tone→color logic (TopologyGraph alone has four parallel maps) in three incompatible expression forms, and the error concept is spelled two ways (bg-destructive vs bg-[var(--red)]) with no lint holding them together. The dataviz half of the design system was generalized into a registry; the status-signal half was not.
audits.ideal: A world-class Dispatch language has exactly one registry per semantic axis, and status signaling is an axis. Mirroring lib/chart-colors.ts, a lib/status-tokens.ts exports the single status→token map (StateDot's STATE_COLORS promoted out of the component) plus thin accessors — statusVar(state) returning `var(--green)` etc., and statusDotClass(state) returning the Tailwind form — so a dot, a badge border, a timeline node, a rail, and a text color all cite one function instead of re-deriving the mapping. StateDot, StatusBadge, TopologyGraph, BriefingStatus, ToolCallTimeline, ButlerHeartbeatTile, BoardFooter, LiveIndicator, qa-patrol-status and the passport atoms all consume it. One spelling wins for each state (canonically var(--red)/--red-text to match the attention-tint rails and StateDot), enforced by an eslint guard that bans the losing form (bg-destructive) exactly as the repo already bans hsl(var()). Dot diameter is a fixed 6px token with at most one named larger variant, so no caller can invent an 8px or 10px dot. The result: one hue, one meaning, one spelling, one accessor, everywhere — a five-second read where green always means healthy through a single code path, and a retune of any state color propagates atomically instead of splitting silently across 40 sites.

findings.title: Empty states rarely teach the action that fills them; several bypass the shared component with ad-hoc strings
findings.evidence: components/ui/empty-state.tsx exists with an `action` slot; only 6 of 19 <EmptyState> call sites pass `action`; ad-hoc bare strings at EntityDetailPage.tsx:288/301/1800/2239, TimelinePage.tsx:357, SessionDetailPage.tsx:31 skip the component entirely
findings.detail: Discoverability bar: 'an empty list shows the action that fills it, not just No items.' Voice-variant surfaces intentionally stay bare (design-language), but page-variant lists with an obvious fill path (add connector, trigger run, link contact) mostly render a dead-end sentence. This is the cross-surface pattern of the shell frame not being consistently applied.

audits.ideal: A world-class operator shell makes participation in its own discovery systems the default, not an opt-in each page re-earns. Every route is one registry entry that simultaneously builds the sidebar, the palette Pages group, the g-chord, and the help sheet (this already exists and is excellent). The ideal extends that single-spine principle to verbs and affordances: a page declares its primary actions once, and that declaration renders the on-page buttons AND the palette Actions AND the '?' hints — they cannot drift because there is one source. Every attention surface (anything the shell badges) is guaranteed a g-chord by a coverage test, and every chord is taught in three places it is used: the palette entry's kbd column, the sidebar row's tooltip, and the help sheet. The palette itself announces its existence with a visible, platform-aware 'Search… ⌘K' pill in the chrome, so the chord is never the only door. Empty states on fillable lists always name the action that fills them. The result: first use needs no docs (visible affordances everywhere), tenth use needs no mouse (complete, advertised chords), and no surface can be built without inheriting the whole discovery frame.
audits.jarvis_gap: The shell has genuinely world-class discovery machinery — route-registry.ts as a single source of truth, split-context command/shortcut registries, the unified EntityFinder palette, a registry-derived help sheet — and it is a large advance over the pre-bu-86c4c drift. But generalization stopped at the plumbing. Verbs reach the palette only from ~10 hand-wired components while the highest-frequency triage pages (Approvals, Decisions, Notifications, Issues, Sessions) register nothing, and the registry's own docstring advertises Approve/Acknowledge examples that were never built. Chords are hand-assigned with a uniqueness test but no coverage test, so the two badged attention surfaces the system pushes you toward have no fast path. And the affordances that teach these systems are missing: the palette entry point is an unlabeled icon with a hover-only tooltip, chords never appear on the nav items they target, and most empty states dead-end. Today is a strong spine with a thin, uneven skin; the ideal is the spine reaching every page and advertising itself at every touch.

findings.title: Freshness policy built as named tokens + bus-aware interval, but ~16 domain hooks still poll on raw literals with no live path and no lint
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:18-21; eslint.config.js:213-228 (POLL_POLICY_FILES scoped to ~9 files, comment: "~140 other refetchInterval call sites across the app" unenforced); hooks/use-health.ts:70..503 (~13 queries each refetchInterval:30_000); hooks/use-system.ts:29-142; hooks/use-finance.ts:30-70; hooks/use-ingestion.ts:97-305; hooks/use-general.ts:35-104; src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:60-75 (EVENT_TYPES has NO health/system/finance/memory/education/travel type, so those domains have no bus event to ride)
findings.detail: The app has two generalizable freshness mechanisms — the fleet event bus + useBusAwarePollInterval (adopted by ~14 hooks: sessions, approvals, spend, notifications, timeline, issues, calendar, butlers) and named poll-policy tokens (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS / POLL_BUS_DOWN_FALLBACK_MS / POLL_RUNNING_SESSION_MS). Both were deliberately scoped to a small blessed set; ~16 hooks (health, system, finance, ingestion, general, audit-log, owntracks, travel, education, memory-reembed, cli-auth, schedules, state) still hard-code bare numeric intervals. Consequences: (a) Health Overview alone fires ~13 independent 30s polls with no coalescing and no bus invalidation; (b) whole domains have no live update path — a health/finance write is invisible until the next fixed tick; (c) intent (primary path vs bus-reconcile safety net) is un-encoded outside the 9 linted files, so a reviewer cannot tell a 60s literal from a bus-covered surface. The lint selector already exists (eslint.config.js:239) but is applied to a whitelist instead of repo-wide with per-line opt-out.

findings.title: Zero route-chunk prefetch anywhere; primary navigation (Sidebar) has no hover/focus prefetch at all
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:2,203,303,672,777 (plain NavLink, no onMouseEnter/onFocus/prefetch handlers — grep for prefetch in components/layout matches only EntityFinder.tsx); frontend/src/lib/prefetch-registry.ts:12-17,205-218 (warms the DATA query cache only, never the JS chunk; covers detail routes + /timeline + /ingestion event, no top-level list pages); router-config.tsx:28-73 (every page is lazy() — cold navigation pays a chunk download); grep for `import(.*pages/` / preload / prefetchRoute across src returns nothing outside lazy() declarations
findings.detail: usePrefetchOnIntent + prefetch-registry warm the TanStack cache for in-content detail rows (RowLink, DisclosureRow, command-palette highlight), which is good. But the single most-travelled surface — the Sidebar — uses plain NavLink and prefetches nothing on hover/focus, and no code anywhere warms a route's lazy chunk. So every first navigation to a cold route is: click → Suspense fallback → chunk fetch → data fetch, serially, with the slow work on the hot path instead of during the hover that precedes it. The perceived-performance program generalized data-prefetch to leaf rows but never to (a) the route chunk or (b) the top-level nav that drives most navigation.

findings.title: No repeat-safe submit primitive: shared Button has no pending affordance; raw <button onClick={()=>mut.mutate()}> sites lack any disabled guard
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/button.tsx:41-60 (no loading/pending prop — only disabled:opacity styling; every call site must hand-wire disabled={mut.isPending}); frontend/src/components/relationship/CirclesPage.tsx:250 (raw <button onClick={() => remove.mutate(...)}> — no disabled); frontend/src/pages/TimelinePage.tsx:320 (deleteSavedView.mutate on raw <button>, no disabled); frontend/src/components/chronicles/WorkScheduleSettings.tsx:341 (del.mutate, raw button)
findings.detail: Repeat-safety (skill: 'a double-click must never double-submit') is opt-in and inconsistent. The shared Button exposes no pending state, so ~349 files hand-wire disabled={isPending}; some (QaStafferCard.tsx:253 disabled={syncRepo.isPending}) do it, others fire mutations from raw <button> elements with no disabled/pending guard at all, so a double-click double-submits. There is no structural guarantee — a `pending` prop on Button that auto-disables+dedupes in-flight, plus a lint ban on raw <button onClick={()=>*.mutate()}>, would make the guarantee structural instead of per-author discipline.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the frontend has world-class interaction-speed *primitives* — a live event bus with a hand-verified cache-coverage manifest, a bus-aware poll interval, named poll-policy tokens, a well-adopted optimistic-mutation family (useOptimisticMutation/useOptimisticListMutation now in ~13 hooks), a debounced global search with a never-blank floor, a hover-intent data-prefetch registry, and 100% route code-splitting with background-poll suppressed globally (query-client.ts:8 refetchIntervalInBackground:false). The in-flight bu-27dxl.13 items (lazy-all routes, background-poll-off, prefetch registry) have measurably landed. The gap to a JARVIS bar is *generalization*: every one of these mechanisms stops at a blessed whitelist. Freshness is bus-aware on ~14 hooks and a raw literal on ~16 (whole domains — health, system, finance — have no live path and no lint). Prefetch warms leaf-row data but never a route chunk and never the primary Sidebar nav. Repeat-safety is hand-wired per button with no shared pending primitive. The ideal is that these become the enforced *default* — a query wrapper that resolves freshness by domain, a nav/route prefetch that warms chunk+data on the highest-traffic surface, and a Button that is repeat-safe by construction — so a new page inherits five-second-snappy behaviour without an author re-discovering the pattern.
audits.ideal: Interaction-speed doctrine is enforced by default, not by whitelist. (1) One `useDomainQuery` freshness resolver classifies every read as bus-covered (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS reconcile-only), poll-primary (named token), or static — a bare numeric refetchInterval is a repo-wide lint error with per-line opt-out, and every domain either emits a bus event or carries an explicit, documented poll token, so no surface silently polls blind. (2) A single `useRoutePrefetch` warms both the lazy route chunk (import()) and its registry data query on hover/focus, wired into the Sidebar NavLinks and generalized through RowLink/DisclosureRow, so the hot path on click is already warm. (3) The shared Button is repeat-safe by construction (a `pending` prop that disables, shows honest progress, and dedupes in-flight), and raw `<button onClick={()=>mut.mutate()}>` is lint-banned. Together these make snappy the inherited default: a new page is bus-fresh, prefetch-warm, and double-submit-proof with zero bespoke wiring.

findings.title: Chronicles Gantt episode bars are keyboard-inoperable SVG click targets
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/GanttSwimlaneInner.tsx:310-316
findings.detail: The primary drill-into-episode affordance in the Chronicles Gantt view is an SVG <g role=button aria-label onClick={handleClick}> with NO tabIndex and NO onKeyDown (it is the only keyboard-relevant marker in GanttSwimlane*.tsx). You cannot Tab to a bar and Enter/Space does nothing, so the drilldown loop is mouse-only. Same-surface inconsistency: the HTML-rendered twin DayRibbon.tsx:177-195 renders the identical affordance as a real <button> with focus-visible:ring-2 and aria-label, fully operable. Every other role=button div in the app (CirclesPage.tsx:365, JsonViewer.tsx:103, EpisodesRegister.tsx:156, SettingsConsolePage.tsx:331) correctly pairs tabIndex+onKeyDown. The global focus floor index.css:617 also cannot help: an SVG <g> with no tabIndex is not focusable so it never gets :focus-visible.

findings.title: Secrets passport strips focus outline on raw inputs/textareas with no ring replacement
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx:1613,2155,2206,3438,3481; ProviderConfigDrawer.tsx:290,308,879,1168; Spine.tsx:53; GoogleAppCredentials.tsx:98
findings.detail: The highest-stakes editing surface (pasting/rotating credentials and secret values) is built from raw <input>/<textarea> carrying outline-none with NO focus-visible ring (e.g. font-mono text-[11px] p-2 resize-none outline-none w-full). Two safety nets both miss: ui/input.tsx:11-12 strips the outline but re-adds focus-visible:ring-[3px] and the passport bypasses that primitive; and the global floor index.css:617 uses selector :where(a, button, [role=button], [tabindex]) which excludes input/textarea/select. Net: keyboard/AT users editing a secret get zero visible focus indicator (WCAG 2.4.7) on the surface where knowing the active field matters most. ~17 fields across 4 files; a whole surface built off-primitive.

findings.title: Five domain data tables use raw <th> with no scope, bypassing the scope-hardened primitive
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerRelationshipContactsTab.tsx:373-376; ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx:389-400; ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:310-314; ButlerHomeDevicesTab.tsx:196-200; ButlerGeneralCollectionsTab.tsx:203-205
findings.detail: The bu-27dxl.11 scope-association move landed only in the shared primitive ui/table.tsx:53-57 (TableHead defaults scope=col) and one hand-maintained panel (approvals/attention-ledger-panel.tsx:88,207 sets scope by hand). Five butler-detail domain tables instead hand-roll raw <table> with bare <th ... font-medium> and no scope, so screen readers cannot associate cells with column headers on the relationship watchlist, finance transactions, QA investigations, home devices and general collections surfaces (the read-heavy domain exploration named in purpose-and-single-pane.md:24). WCAG 1.3.1; the fixing primitive already exists but was never adopted.

audits.ideal: One accessibility floor that is structurally impossible to fall through, reaching every rendering technology equally. Interactivity is expressed through a single vocabulary of primitives (ui/button, ui/input, ui/table, DisclosureRow, plus a still-missing SVG/canvas-mark equivalent) each baking in the full keyboard+focus+semantics contract (role, tabIndex, Enter/Space activation, a visible focus ring, accessible name, header scope) so no author can hand-build a click-only or focus-invisible control. Where a surface legitimately needs bespoke markup (SVG timelines, secret editors), the global CSS focus floor covers it because its selector spans every focusable element type, and an eslint a11y ruleset (raw th must carry scope; role=button requires tabIndex+onKeyDown; raw input/textarea with outline-none is banned) makes regressions fail CI rather than ship. Reduced motion, skip link, and the shell aria-live announcer are the model: floors defined once, applied globally, verified by test. Every hot loop is completed mouse-unplugged with a focus ring the whole way.
audits.jarvis_gap: The shell floor genuinely generalized: the global reduced-motion collapse (index.css:785), skip link and sr-only shell announcer (RootLayout.tsx:99-100,44), scope-defaulting TableHead (ui/table.tsx:53), the focus-visible global rule (index.css:617), and the input primitive ring (ui/input.tsx:12) are all real and correct, and PlexPage (real button nodes with focus/blur parity, role=application canvas keyboard handling) shows the bar is understood. But the floor stops at the edge of the shared primitives: the moment a surface hand-rolls markup it silently drops below WCAG AA. SVG interactive marks have no primitive, so the Chronicles Gantt bar is click-only while its HTML twin DayRibbon is a proper button; the global focus selector was scoped to exclude form controls, so the secrets passport's ~17 raw inputs edit credentials with no focus ring; and the scope move reached the primitive but not the five butler-detail tables that never adopted it. The gap is not missing floors but that they are opt-in by construction (a primitive you must choose to import, a CSS selector listing element types by hand) rather than enforced by a lint gate, so each new hand-built surface reintroduces the same three defects.

A shared interactiveMarkProps({label,onActivate}) returning role+tabIndex=0+onKeyDown(Enter/Space)+onClick+aria-label, applied to the <g>, closes the Chronicles drilldown loop and gives future SVG timelines one correct source.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the butlers perceive the owner's world almost entirely through two lenses: passive email parsing (Finance, Travel) and a fixed set of streaming/social/location connectors (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Health-aggregate, Home Assistant, OwnTracks, Spotify, Steam, Discord/Telegram/WhatsApp). The two most value-dense butlers — Finance and Travel — literally define themselves as "we read your email so you don't have to" (roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md, roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md), which means their ground truth is only as complete as what merchants and airlines happen to email. Finance ingestion is CSV/email only with NO live account feed (openspec/specs/finance-data-import/spec.md is entirely bank-CSV-format detection). Health perception stops at Google Health's step/weight aggregation with no wearable readiness/sleep/HRV signal. Home promises to act on "air quality" and "conditions drift" (roster/home/MANIFESTO.md) but has no environmental/weather feed — only Home Assistant device state. Chronicler builds a daily narrative but cannot see photographic evidence of the day. A world-class JARVIS perceives from authoritative source-of-record APIs (the bank, the airline's live ops feed, the wearable, the atmosphere, the camera roll), not from the incidental exhaust that lands in an inbox. bu-27dxl.15 already extends perception into GitHub/podcasts/YouTube/reading; the gap below is the higher-value tier of owner-life signal those don't touch.

moves.title: Live bank/card aggregator connector (SimpleFIN Bridge, Plaid-optional)
moves.why: Finance's manifesto promises 'financial clarity automatically, every morning' (roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md) but its only ingestion is email receipts + manual CSV import (openspec/specs/finance-data-import/spec.md, openspec/specs/bulk-transaction-ingestion). Email misses every non-emailing merchant, cash-app/Zelle transfer, and any card the owner didn't route mail for — the ledger is silently incomplete, which violates the vision's 'nothing fabricated / staleness never wears current-data authority' bar (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md) because a partial ledger renders as a complete one. A read-only account aggregator (SimpleFIN Bridge is single-owner-friendly and token-based; Plaid a heavier alt) turns the transaction feed authoritative. Payoff: the 'what did I spend on restaurants' answer becomes truly complete and same-day, and duplicate email-vs-feed receipts reconcile against one canonical row.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/simplefin.py following connector-base-spec (ingest.v1 envelopes -> Switchboard); new spec openspec/specs/connector-simplefin + finance-data-import extension for feed-vs-email dedup; account registry entry (pattern of steam-account-registry / google-account-registry) storing the SimpleFIN access URL in butler_secrets; finance.transactions as the sink with a source='aggregator' provenance column so email-derived and feed-derived rows are distinguishable and reconcilable.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: registry + connector polling one account into finance.transactions with provenance tag (no dedup). Slice 2: reconcile feed rows against existing email/CSV rows on (amount, date, merchant-fuzzy). Slice 3: dashboard finance surface shows per-account feed freshness + degraded flag when the aggregator token is stale (fabricated-calm guard).

moves.title: Real-time flight/itinerary status connector (TripIt-import or AeroDataBox/AviationStack)
moves.why: Travel's manifesto explicitly promises trips that are 'synced, real-time, and ready' and that 'check-in windows' and 'itinerary changes' never pass unnoticed (roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md) — but today the only source is booking-confirmation emails, which are static and never reflect a live delay, gate change, or cancellation. That is exactly the 'staleness wearing current-data authority' failure the vision forbids (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md): the dashboard shows a 3:40pm departure the airline has already slipped to 6:10pm. A flight-status connector keyed off the flight numbers Travel already extracts closes the loop from 'I recorded your booking' to 'your gate just changed.' Payoff: proactive delay/gate/cancellation notifications and an itinerary that matches reality at the airport.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/flight_status.py; new spec openspec/specs/connector-flight-status; reads travel-butler's trip/segment schema for active flight numbers, polls a flight-data API, emits ingest.v1 status-change events -> Switchboard -> travel butler -> core-notify. TripIt Inbound (forward confirmations, get structured itineraries) is a lower-cost alternative source; AeroDataBox/AviationStack for live status. Reuses the deadline-tracking spec for check-in windows.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: poll live status for flights already in the trip schema, notify on delta > threshold. Slice 2: TripIt inbound as a richer confirmation parser feeding the same trip schema. Slice 3: gate/seat/baggage-belt enrichment on the trip detail page.

moves.title: Wearable readiness connector (Oura / Whoop)
moves.why: Health's manifesto commits to 'the full picture of your wellbeing' as a story told 'over weeks, months, and years' (roster/health/MANIFESTO.md), but the only automated feed is Google Health (openspec/specs/connector-google-health, module-google-health) which aggregates steps/weight — it has no sleep architecture, HRV, resting-HR trend, or recovery/readiness score. Those are the signals that actually let a health companion 'help you see what you might otherwise miss.' A wearable connector adds the daily physiological ground truth that makes proactive insight (openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine, seasonal-awareness) real rather than step-count-shaped. Payoff: 'your readiness has been trending down for 5 days and you slept 5h last night' — the kind of noticing JARVIS is for.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/oura.py mirroring the google_health.py client+connector split; OAuth via the account-registry pattern; new spec openspec/specs/connector-oura + module-google-health-parallel health module tools for readiness/sleep/HRV; sinks into the health butler schema alongside existing google-health metrics so the health overview (dashboard-domain-pages) can trend them together.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: OAuth + daily sleep/readiness/HRV pull into health tables. Slice 2: health overview trend cards + proactive-insight rule on multi-day decline. Slice 3: correlate with calendar load / activitywatch focus for 'busy week -> poor recovery' narrative.

moves.title: Environment connector: weather + air quality + pollen (Pirate Weather / PurpleAir / OpenWeather)
moves.why: Home's manifesto promises to act when 'conditions drift outside your comfort zone' including 'air quality' (roster/home/MANIFESTO.md), yet Home only sees Home Assistant device state (openspec/specs/connector-home-assistant) — it has no exogenous atmosphere signal, so it can react to an indoor sensor but never anticipate ('AQI hits 160 this afternoon, close the windows and run the purifier'). This single cheap feed is cross-butler leverage: Home for comfort/pre-conditioning, Health for pollen/AQI advisories, Travel for weather-at-destination. It directly serves the vision's proactive, 'before you have to ask' posture (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md) at minimal cost.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/weather.py (no OAuth — API key in butler_secrets); new spec openspec/specs/connector-weather; emits ingest.v1 forecast/AQI/pollen events -> Switchboard -> fan-out to home (comfort pre-conditioning rules, home-deterministic-jobs), health (advisory), travel (destination outlook). Keyed off OwnTracks/home location so it self-configures.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: current + forecast + AQI for the owner's home location into a shared context table. Slice 2: home comfort/pre-conditioning trigger rules. Slice 3: pollen/AQI health advisory + travel destination weather on the trip page.

moves.title: Photo-memory connector (Google Photos / Immich) for Chronicler
moves.why: Chronicler builds the day's narrative from intent/evidence/activity signals (openspec/specs/chronicler-intent-evidence-activity, chronicler-source-compatibility) but is blind to the single richest human record of a day — the photos taken. A photo-memory connector gives the daily story real evidence anchors ('you were at the coast at 4pm — 6 photos') and lets the chronicler's narrative-truth work (bu-27dxl.1) stand on artifacts rather than inferred activity. Reuses the existing Google OAuth registry, so incremental cost is low. Payoff: chronicles that show, not just tell, and a searchable 'what was I doing when' spine.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/google_photos.py reusing google-account-registry + google-multi-account-oauth (same pattern as connectors/google_drive.py); new spec openspec/specs/connector-google-photos; emits media-evidence events (timestamp, geo, thumbnail ref, S3 blob via s3-blob-storage spec) as chronicler activity evidence; feeds chronicler-api / dashboard-chronicles as photo evidence tiles. Immich as a self-hosted privacy alternative behind the same connector interface.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: pull photo metadata (time/geo, no full media) as chronicler evidence rows. Slice 2: thumbnail blobs via s3-blob-storage for the chronicles timeline. Slice 3: cross-link photos to calendar events / owntracks places for narrative anchoring.

moves.title: Package/shipment tracking connector (carrier APIs via 17track/AfterShip, or structured order-email parse)
moves.why: 'Where is my package / did it arrive' is a daily owner question no butler can answer today. Delivery-confirmation and shipping emails already land in Gmail but are parsed by nobody — this is latent perception the ecosystem drops on the floor. It serves the General 'second brain' promise (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md) of not having to track where things are, and the vision's proactive posture (a porch-pirate-prone package arriving while you're out is exactly a 'notice before you ask' moment). Because no current manifesto squarely owns physical logistics, this implies either a General-butler manifesto amendment ('we track what's coming to you') or a small dedicated concern — flag that decision explicitly rather than smuggling scope.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/shipments.py; either (a) an aggregator API (17track/AfterShip) keyed off tracking numbers, or (b) a Gmail-derived parser that extracts tracking numbers from shipping emails (reuses connector-gmail ingest) then resolves status. New spec openspec/specs/connector-shipments; sinks to a general/lifestyle schema table with delivery-ETA; core-notify on out-for-delivery/delivered/exception. Requires a manifesto decision: amend roster/general/MANIFESTO.md to own inbound logistics, or scope to lifestyle.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: Gmail-derived tracking-number extraction + status resolution (no new external account). Slice 2: delivery-ETA + out-for-delivery/exception notifications. Slice 3: a lightweight 'incoming' surface on the owning butler's dashboard page. Gate on the manifesto-ownership decision first.

findings.title: Every spawn re-sends the full butler system prompt; no provider session reuse
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1512-1513 (system_prompt passed fresh every invoke); grep for resume/--session/continue in src/butlers/core/adapters/ and runtimes/ returns nothing

No adapter passes a provider resume/session handle, so multi-turn conversations (Telegram/chat) cold-start each turn, re-paying full system-prompt input tokens and discarding provider prompt-cache warmth.

findings.title: Routing/breaker ignore latency; model_dispatch_attempts stores no duration

A working-but-slow model (cf. the 436s opencode incident in openspec/specs/runtime-opencode/spec.md) is never penalized; equal-priority ties fall to blind round-robin, not a cost/latency/success score.

findings.evidence: model_routing.py:361 (_BREAKER_OPEN_CTE deliberately unfiltered, comment at 384-393); resolve path then _SPEND_RULES_SELECT_SQL (740), _RESOLVE_BY_MODEL_ID_SQL (751), get_breaker_state (420), _QUOTA_CHECK_SQL (667), _CEILING_SELECT_SQL (716)

Serialized latency plus recurring load on the fragile shared Postgres/Dolt plane.

findings.title: Switchboard pays a cheap-tier routing LLM roundtrip per inbound with no decision memoization
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/complexity-classification/spec.md 'Switchboard Complexity Classification' (piggybacks on routing LLM call); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py classification spawn (trigger_source=classification, cheap tier)
findings.detail: Deterministic triage exists (rule/thread-affinity, ingestion-policy) but any message that misses it pays a full cheap-tier LLM classification, including repeated/near-identical prompts. No bounded recent-decision cache keyed on normalized message+sender.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the trigger->spawn->act loop is correct and well-instrumented but latency- and cost-naive. Routing selects by capability tier + static priority + a failure-only circuit breaker (model_routing.py _BREAKER_OPEN_CTE), never by observed latency or cost-efficiency, even though duration_ms is already measured (spawner.py:1827) and simply discarded from the dispatch trail. Every spawn is a cold ephemeral CLI that re-sends the full butler system prompt (spawner.py:1512) with no provider session resume (adapters have none), so multi-turn conversation re-pays system-prompt tokens and loses prompt-cache warmth turn after turn. The switchboard already knows the target butler and complexity from its cheap-tier classification LLM call, yet MCP/codex warmup happens lazily at spawn time on the critical path (spawner _ensure_mcp_endpoints_warmed, codex run_codex_pre_warm) rather than speculatively during classification. And the pre-spawn gate stack fires 5-6 serial DB round-trips (one an unfiltered full-table window scan) before a single token is generated. A JARVIS-grade loop would route on a live cost x latency x success score, resume provider sessions for conversation, prewarm speculatively off the classification decision, memoize idempotent decisions honestly, and collapse the gate chain into one round-trip.
audits.ideal: The ideal inference loop treats latency and money as first-class routing signals under the earned-calm north star: models are ranked by a live, honest cost x latency x success score (not blind round-robin), the same trigger reuses a warm provider session across conversational turns instead of cold-starting, the switchboard classification decision speculatively prewarms the chosen butler's runtime so the act-spawn begins warm, idempotent read-only decisions are memoized with explicit staleness labels that never impersonate fresh data, and the pre-spawn authorization/budget gate resolves in a single index-bound round-trip. First-token output streams to interactive owner surfaces so perceived latency collapses. Every one of these is measurable on the existing dispatch/ledger spine, so the speedups are provable rather than asserted.

findings.title: Insight digest is a flat numbered list — no cross-butler synthesis
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/insight-delivery/spec.md:336-345 (digest = numbered list, origin butler in brackets); proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:279-295 (dedup only collapses identical dedup_keys)
findings.detail: The one place the whole fleet's output converges (the daily digest) does zero synthesis. Correlated-but-distinct candidates (Travel 'Tokyo Tue', Finance 'balance low', Health 'vaccination due before travel', Calendar 'deadline Wed') are emitted as N separate bullets; the owner must assemble the meaning. Dedup collapses exact key matches but cannot see that four candidates share an entity/time window. This is the single-pane doctrine (docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md) violated at the notification layer — the fleet knows the whole picture, the owner is handed fragments.

findings.title: Cross-butler interaction is one-shot pull only; no standing subscription primitive
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:13-45 (ask->resolve->answer, one row per question); context-bus/spec.md:107-133 (fixed 11-signal user-state vocabulary, hardcoded writers)
findings.detail: A butler can ASK another a question once (delegation), or READ a fixed user-state signal (context bus, vocabulary frozen at traveling/sleeping/meeting/...). Neither lets butler A durably WATCH butler B's domain — 'tell me whenever a trip is booked', 'tell me when a large transaction lands'. There is no domain-event bus and no subscription table. Genuine collaboration (Finance pre-budgeting a trip the moment Travel books it) is structurally impossible today.

findings.title: No multi-butler workflow primitive — coordination is passive date-keyed fan-in
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/cross-butler-briefing-aggregation/spec.md:438-461 (General reads a read-only view of each schema's briefing/daily/% state and merges by date)
findings.detail: The only cross-butler assembly that exists is the morning briefing: a passive UNION view keyed on today's date. There is no durable object representing a multi-domain objective ('moving apartments', 'recovering from surgery', 'planning the trip') that several butlers own steps of, with dependencies and completion tracking. Multi-butler goals that require sequenced contribution have nowhere to live.

findings.title: Insight broker cannot detect semantic conflict between distinct candidates
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:279-307 (dedup by identical dedup_key; budget selection is pure descending-priority)
findings.detail: Two butlers can hold contradictory intents (Finance: 'cut discretionary spend'; Travel: 'book the trip you saved') under different dedup_keys. The broker treats them as independent, ranks by priority, and may deliver both or neither — never surfaces the tension as one decision. Contradiction is invisible to the coordination layer.

audits.ideal: Butlers should be able to collaborate as a team, not just answer each other's one-off questions. The ideal is four missing primitives layered on the existing MCP-only, Switchboard-brokered spine: (1) a durable domain-event bus so any butler can publish 'a thing happened in my domain' and others can hold standing subscriptions — pub/sub, not just ask/answer; (2) a mission object that represents a cross-domain objective the owner is pursuing, decomposed into steps each butler owns with dependencies, coordinated by a Chief-of-Staff role, so 'plan the move' becomes one tracked plan instead of seven disconnected sessions; (3) a synthesis pass at the fleet's convergence point (the daily digest and any multi-source card) that clusters correlated candidates by shared entity and time window and hands the owner one coherent narrative, not a fragment list; (4) an attention/time-budget broker mirroring the proven insight-budget broker, so butlers competing for the owner's finite calendar time and daily attention negotiate through a single allocator instead of each writing independently. Every one of these routes through the Switchboard and public-schema shared tables — no new inter-butler side channel, honoring non-negotiable rule 3. The result: the fleet accomplishes things no single butler can — a Tokyo trip where Finance has pre-budgeted, Health has flagged the vaccination, and Calendar has protected the deadline, delivered as one calm heads-up.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today cross-butler interaction is three narrow, mostly one-directional mechanisms: the situational context bus (a frozen 11-signal user-STATE vocabulary with hardcoded writers, context-bus/spec.md:107-133), the insight engine (butler->user proposals that dedup and digest but never synthesize, insight-delivery/spec.md:336-345), and the in-flight delegation ledger (one butler asks one resolved butler one question, cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:13-45; wake-loop is bu-27dxl.5). Butlers cannot watch each other's domains, cannot share a multi-step objective, cannot have their overlapping signals synthesized into one story, and cannot negotiate for the owner's finite time — they each act alone and the owner does the integration. A JARVIS is a chief of staff coordinating specialists toward the owner's goals; the Butlers fleet is currently seven specialists filing independent reports past each other.

moves.title: Domain-event bus: standing cross-butler subscriptions (pub/sub beyond ask/answer)
moves.why: architecture.md:30-54 makes MCP-through-Switchboard the only sanctioned coordination channel, and vision.md:8-11 charges the Switchboard with 'shared situational awareness so butlers adapt to the user's current context.' Today that awareness is a frozen 11-signal user-STATE vocabulary (context-bus/spec.md:107-133) — there is no way for Finance to say 'wake me when Travel books a trip' or Health to say 'wake me when a trip goes active so I can front-load medication reminders.' Delegation (cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:13-45) is one-shot pull. A durable publish/subscribe log turns the fleet reactive: butlers pre-empt each other's needs the moment a domain event fires. Payoff: the owner never has to be the message-passer between domains — booking a trip silently triggers budget, vaccination, and packing prep.
moves.integration_points: New public.domain_events append log (id, source_butler, event_type, entity_id, payload jsonb, occurred_at) + public.butler_subscriptions (subscriber_butler, event_type_glob, delivery=wake|digest). Switchboard gains publish_domain_event + subscribe MCP tools and a fan-out worker that route()s matched events to each subscriber's new on_domain_event tool (reuse the delegate wake-routing plumbing from bu-27dxl.5). New openspec change 'cross-butler-domain-event-bus'. This is the general pub/sub layer the fixed context bus should have been.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: schema + publish/subscribe tools + Switchboard fan-out worker, wired to ONE real pair (Travel trip-booked -> Finance pre-budget) end to end with an integration test. Slice 2: subscription management UI + a second consumer (Health medication front-load). Slice 3: retire the redundant context-bus deterministic producers that a domain-event subscription now subsumes.

moves.title: Cross-domain missions: a Chief-of-Staff object for multi-butler objectives
moves.why: vision.md:120-126 defines success as 'the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs' and architecture.md:64-86 insists on domain specialization — but the corollary, that some owner goals span every domain, has no home. The only cross-butler assembly today is a passive date-keyed briefing UNION (cross-butler-briefing-aggregation/spec.md:438-461). A mission ('moving apartments', 'recovering from surgery', 'the Japan trip') decomposed into owned, dependency-linked steps, coordinated by a Chief-of-Staff, is the clearest 'accomplish what none can alone.' Payoff: the owner states a goal once and watches the fleet drive it to completion instead of hand-carrying context between seven butlers.
moves.integration_points: New public.missions + public.mission_steps (owner_butler, depends_on[], status, evidence_ref). A coordinator job (Switchboard staffer, or a new 'concierge' staffer) advances the DAG: when a step's deps are satisfied it route()s a prompt to the owning butler; butlers report via mission_step_complete. This has NO manifesto today — General's is a personal second-brain (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md), not a coordinator — so it implies either a Switchboard infrastructure-contract amendment or a NEW 'Chief-of-Staff' staffer manifesto. New openspec change 'cross-butler-missions'. Dashboard: a mission detail page (detail-page-archetype spec).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: schema + coordinator DAG-advance job + mission_step_complete, hardcoded template for ONE mission type (a trip: travel->finance->health->calendar) proven end to end. Slice 2: mission list/detail dashboard surface with per-step evidence spine. Slice 3: owner-initiated mission creation via chat/telegram + LLM decomposition into steps.

moves.title: Fleet insight synthesis: cluster correlated candidates into one narrative before delivery
moves.why: docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md's single-pane mandate and the earned-calm north star both demand the owner receive meaning, not fragments — yet the fleet's convergence point emits a flat numbered list (insight-delivery/spec.md:336-345) and dedup only collapses identical keys (proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:279-295). No single butler can see that 'Tokyo Tuesday' + 'balance low' + 'vaccination due' + 'deadline Wed' are one situation; the broker CAN, because it holds all candidates. Payoff: instead of four bullets the owner reads 'Heads-up on your Tokyo trip Tuesday: money's tight, you need a vaccination first, and there's a deadline the day you're back' — genuine collaboration surfacing.
moves.integration_points: Extend the Switchboard insight broker delivery cycle (proactive-insight-engine): after budget selection, an LLM synthesis pass clusters winning insight_candidates by shared entity_id / overlapping time window (both already available in candidate metadata + dedup_key convention {category}:{entity}:{time-scope}, spec.md:292-295) and composes a coherent digest. Add intent='insight' synthesis rendering. Amends proactive-insight-engine + insight-delivery specs. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (its insight-broker responsibility).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: deterministic clustering by exact entity_id + time-window overlap, deliver each cluster as a labeled sub-group in the existing digest (zero LLM). Slice 2: LLM synthesis of each cluster into one sentence, gated behind the same budget. Slice 3: cross-cluster conflict flag (Finance 'don't spend' vs Travel 'book it') routed to the Owner Decision Desk (bu-ckkpz) as a single tension decision rather than two contradictory bullets.

moves.title: Cross-butler entity dossier: on-demand fleet-wide fan-out for one entity
moves.why: vision.md:15-20 makes each butler a specialist holding one facet of the owner's life; architecture.md:319-344 anchors shared identity in public.entities. When the owner asks about a person/place/trip, every butler holds a fragment (Relationship: who they are and last contact; Finance: money owed; Calendar: upcoming events; Health: n/a) and there is no primitive to assemble them — delegation (cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:13-45) resolves to and asks exactly ONE butler. Payoff: 'what's the story with Sarah?' returns a unified card — relationship tier, outstanding loan, next scheduled meeting — that no single butler could produce.
moves.integration_points: New Switchboard entity_dossier(entity_id) tool that fans out route() calls to each butler's new entity_summary(entity_id) tool (butlers that hold nothing return empty; classify absent-vs-failed per the degraded-source doctrine in butlers/CLAUDE.md). Anchored on public.entities. Distinct from the KG provenance work (bu-27dxl.4, which is per-fact evidence/graph-health, not an on-demand fan-out). New openspec change 'cross-butler-entity-dossier'. Dashboard: entity detail page aggregation. Serves the Switchboard contract + every domain manifesto's entity view.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: entity_summary tool on Relationship + Finance + General (calendar) only, entity_dossier fan-out with degraded-source flags, proven for one entity. Slice 2: dashboard entity dossier card. Slice 3: expose dossier to butler LLM sessions so any butler can pull cross-domain context on an entity mid-reasoning.

moves.title: Attention-budget broker: butlers negotiate for the owner's finite calendar time
moves.why: vision.md:135-137 ('surface timely insights... automatically reduce frequency when the owner disengages') and the earned-calm north star treat the owner's attention as the scarce resource the whole system must respect. The insight engine already proves the pattern — a global daily DELIVERY budget butlers cannot bypass (proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:301-318). But calendar time has no equivalent: Health wants exercise blocks, Education wants study blocks, Relationship wants reach-out reminders, and each writes to the shared butler calendar independently with only pairwise 'suggest' conflict handling (shared/AGENTS.md Calendar Usage). No component allocates the owner's finite free time ACROSS competing butlers. Payoff: the fleet proposes a balanced week instead of seven butlers each grabbing slots first-come.
moves.integration_points: New public.time_block_requests (requesting_butler, domain, priority, duration, window, flexibility) + a Switchboard/General broker job that allocates requests against the owner's actual free calendar and a daily time-budget, mirroring insight-broker selection (descending priority, budget cap). Butlers stop writing calendar blocks directly and instead submit requests. New openspec change 'attention-time-budget-broker'; amends the calendar write contract in shared/AGENTS.md. Serves Health/Education/Relationship/Lifestyle manifestos jointly.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: request table + broker allocating against free/busy for TWO competing butlers (Health exercise vs Education study), deterministic priority. Slice 2: migrate remaining butler calendar writers onto request submission. Slice 3: adaptive budget that shrinks on owner disengagement, reusing the insight engine's disengagement ratchet (insight-delivery/spec.md:391-395).

moves.title: Derived-advisory read layer: generalize the context bus from user-state to domain advisories
moves.why: architecture.md:374-379 frames the context bus as a pull-based shared-awareness layer butlers 'read before acting' — but its vocabulary is frozen to 11 user-STATE signals with hardcoded writers (context-bus/spec.md:107-133). Real collaboration needs butlers to publish DERIVED advisories for each other: Finance computes 'discretionary budget remaining = low' so Travel/Lifestyle read it before proposing spend; Health computes 'recovery state = depleted' so Lifestyle/General read it before scheduling. Payoff: butlers stop proposing things that contradict the owner's real constraints because the constraint is one authoritative read away, not a delegation round-trip.
moves.integration_points: Generalize public.user_context into (or add alongside) public.domain_advisories keyed on (publishing_butler, advisory_type, value, confidence, TTL) reusing the exact TTL/confidence/supersession model already specced (context-bus/spec.md:148-163), but with an open, butler-declared advisory namespace instead of the fixed ContextSignal enum + write-permission matrix. Read via a consult_advisories MCP tool available to all butlers. Amends context-bus spec. Serves Finance and Health manifestos as publishers; every planning butler as reader.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: advisory table + set/consult tools, Finance publishes budget_pressure, ONE reader (Lifestyle) consults before proposing discretionary spend, integration-tested. Slice 2: Health recovery-state advisory + General/Lifestyle scheduling consult. Slice 3: fold the four fixed context-bus deterministic producers (context-bus-producers/spec.md:168-227) into the general advisory model, retiring the hardcoded write-permission matrix.

audits.ideal: A trustworthy graph grows by earning trust, not by accumulating rows. Every durable fact carries not just its provenance spine (bu-27dxl.4) but three live trust signals the system computes continuously: utility (was this knowledge actually recalled and did the session go well), corroboration (how many independent sources/sessions assert it), and reachability (does another domain need it). Decay stops being silent erosion and becomes active maintenance: high-value knowledge that goes stale asks the owner 'still true?' rather than quietly fading, while single-source, never-recalled claims fade fastest. The predicate vocabulary stays bounded and aggregatable through a promotion loop, and per-entity fact sets stay sharp through salience compaction so retrieval scales. Cross-butler reads happen at zero LLM spend through narrow, sensitivity-ceilinged, entity-keyed read views (RFC 0010), turning 'shared situational awareness' from consumer plumbing into a real deterministic fabric. Trust becomes a computed property with an unbroken trace, never an assertion.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the graph grows but does not learn what to trust or keep. Facts freeze their importance at write time and get zero feedback from being used (storage.py:1809 tracks usage only for predicates, never facts; search.py scoring never reads usage), so pruning and salience are blind. Confirmation only resets a decay clock (storage.py:2478) with no corroboration axis, so five independent assertions decay exactly like one guess. Decay is passive: a high-value fact about an inner-circle person erodes silently instead of prompting re-verification. Cross-butler knowledge sharing is either a summary catalog hit or a full LLM delegation session; there is no zero-spend structured read of a shared-entity fact, so the vision's shared situational awareness stays half-built. Predicates enter as 'proposed' (storage.py:1786) and no loop ever promotes them, so edge vocabulary rots. bu-27dxl.4 lays the provenance evidence/edges/health spine; the growth-and-trust mechanisms that ride on top of that spine are absent.

A fact repeatedly injected into memory_context earns no signal back; the graph cannot tell load-bearing knowledge from write-once noise, so pruning and salience are blind.

findings.evidence: docs/modules/memory.md:194; openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md; grep: zero cross-schema fact views

RFC 0010 already permits narrow read-only views.
